title: Spring AI Landscape & Versions
objective: After this lesson you will be able to map Spring AI's pieces (ChatClient, advisors, RAG, tools, eval, observability, MCP starters), choose starters per need, and pin versions with upgrade awareness.
why: Spring AI is an ecosystem, not a library: models, advisors, vector stores, tools, MCP starters, observability — each with starters and versions. Teams fail by grabbing all starters (dependency sprawl) or none (hand-rolled HTTP). Landscape fluency (what exists, what each piece owns, what versions assume) precedes every build decision in this course.

blocks.text: **ChatClient**: fluent model access (prompts, entities, streaming). **Advisors**: composable interceptors (memory, RAG, logging, tool-calling). **Models**: chat/embedding/image/audio per provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, PostgresML…). **Vector stores**: pgvector/Chroma/MongoDB/etc. behind one interface. **Tools**: POJO methods as model tools. **MCP starters**: client/server boot integration. **Observability/eval**: Micrometer observations, logger advisors, Testcontainers patterns.

This course verified against **Spring AI 2.0.1 reference, Spring Boot 3.x, Java 17+**: ChatClient fluent shapes, advisor ordering semantics, ToolCallingAdvisor auto-registration, entity() switches, StTemplateRenderer defaults all confirmed there. v1→v2 migrations (package moves, advisor builders) get explicit notes where shapes changed. Pin versions in build files; read upgrade notes per minor — AI libraries move quarterly.

blocks.title: Docs-first habit
blocks.text: Spring AI moves quarterly: before trusting any API shape in this course (or elsewhere), check it against the current reference — the version basis above tells you exactly which reference. Shapes confirmed here were verified against 2.0.1; your project's pinned version is the final authority.

blocks.title: Choose the starters
blocks.note: Run it: chat-only stays minimal (2 starters); full RAG service pulls five. Starters follow needs, never FOMO — each dependency is maintenance surface.

items: Pieces own jobs: ChatClient access, advisors interception, stores behind one interface, starters per need
Version basis Spring AI 1.1+/2.x (verified 2.0.1), Boot 3.x, Java 17+ — pin and read upgrade notes
Starters follow needs; minimal viable dependencies, never FOMO sprawl

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice selector for chat-only vs full-service and compare counts. (b) Map your capstone project to starters with one-line need each. (c) State the version-pinning rule (what pins, where, what breaks unpinned in 6 months).
hints: Counts: 2 vs 5 — each starter traces to a need, none to fashion.
Capstone mapping: model starter (chat), pgvector (RAG), testcontainers (eval), micrometer (obs) — MCP starter only if exposing servers.
Pin: BOM + plugin versions in build files; unpinned AI deps drift quarterly into breaking shapes.
exercise.why: Needs-driven dependencies (counted, justified) plus version discipline (pinned, upgrade-read) are the two scaffolding judgments — each verified before any AI code exists.
exercise.code: // Starter-selection pattern: needs in, minimal starters out.

options: Needs-driven minimum: model starter + additions per proven need (RAG→vector store, eval→testcontainers)
quiz.explain: Dependencies are maintenance surface: each starter earns inclusion via a need. Sprawled starters rot unmaintained.

quiz.q: Unpinned Spring AI version for a year. Risk?
options: Quarterly drift into breaking shapes (advisor APIs, package moves) — pin BOM/versions, read upgrade notes per minor
quiz.explain: Fast-moving AI libraries break shapes regularly. Pins + upgrade notes convert surprise into planned work.

quiz.q: MCP server need arises mid-project. Addition?
options: mcp server boot starter (stdio/SSE/streamable variants per Ch.8) — needs-driven, not upfront
quiz.explain: Starters arrive with needs: MCP exposure need → MCP starter. Upfront speculation wastes; just-in-time addition fits.

summary: Landscape mapped (pieces own jobs), versions pinned (2.0.1-verified basis), starters needs-driven. Scaffolding before code, always.
